notes: A brute-force oracle independently re-derives every feature point from the public permutation table and scans a provably sufficient 9^N neighbourhood; it matches optimized 2D/3D f1, f2, nearest offset and feature id bit-for-bit across generated negative, boundary-adjacent and large coordinates for several seeds, plus an adversarial lattice-corner scan that requires the exact ring expansion beyond 3^N.

Unit tests pin seeded fixtures, seed sensitivity, f1 <= f2 ordering, zero f1 at feature points, in-cell feature placement, per-period id uniqueness, 256-cell periodicity, large-coordinate locality and non-finite rejection. A dedicated allocation regression executes 4,096 2D and 3D samples, including ring-expansion inputs, with zero allocation or reallocation calls.
criterion: Allocation-profiled Divan workloads cover scattered and coherent-grid 2D and 3D sampling at multiple sizes.
